A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DAViD and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–C. The complete material supports comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original HOI generation results, a qualitative SGS ablation in Figure 6, and a quantitative comparison with OMOMO in Table 1.

after.justification: V2 reports original HOI comparisons and guidance/LoRA ablations in Tables 1–2, plus object-pose recovery results on BEHAVE in Appendix B.2 and Table 3.

M1.justification: V2 extends smoothness-only SGS into TGS with additional contact guidance and adds a COAP collision penalty to scale optimization. It changes pose normalization from the mean of sampled human vertices to the pelvis joint, and revises LoRA training prompts to category tags with optional left/right annotations. These modify training and inference procedures. The underlying LoRA and pose-diffusion architectures remain; 6D rotation was already documented in v1's appendix.

E1.justification: V2 adds explicit HumanML3D text-conditioned motion evaluation and object-pose recovery evaluation on real BEHAVE video sequences. These introduce tasks beyond v1's use of HumanML3D preprocessing and BEHAVE object meshes. Figure 5 also tests different compositions, including jumping with an umbrella and walking with a suitcase and umbrella. Trumpet and cello examples move from the appendix to Figure 4.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands the evaluated comparator set from OMOMO to OMOMO, CHOIS, and MDM, with MDM evaluated only for human-motion metrics. Appendix B.2 adds FoundationPose with estimated depth as an object-pose recovery comparator. CHOIS was cited in v1 but did not participate in its reported comparison.

E3.justification: V1's mop comparison uses synthetic-trained generation and aggregate wrist-contact SIM/MAE. V2 conditions object generation on test human motions, uses baseline-specific test subsets cropped to contact intervals, and evaluates contact precision/recall/F1 using 25 hand joints and a 0.06 threshold. Human-motion evaluation now trains DAViD on FullBodyManipulation and matches test sample counts. New protocols include the 1000-epoch LoRA retention test and BEHAVE ADD/ADD-S evaluation. Appendix A.6 revises training sample ranges from 5–15 to 5–50 motions and 765–2,295 to 765–7,650 pose pairs.

E4.justification: V1 provides a qualitative SGS ablation. V2 separately examines smoothness and contact guidance in Figure 6, adds quantitative contact ablations in Table 1 and object-jitter measurements in Table 2, and introduces a LoRA versus no-LoRA study of retained motion quality and diversity. These substantially expand the evidence testing design choices.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeat-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. V2's additional sample counts and point-estimate tables do not change uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: V1's Table 1 results are replaced under different conditions, preventing direct version-to-version performance comparisons. V2 reports full-model F1 scores of 0.698 versus CHOIS's 0.565 and 0.667 versus OMOMO's 0.644 in their respective test settings. New results include jitter of 30.9 versus 2.95×10^3 without smoothness guidance, FID of 1.30 versus 2.93 without LoRA, and BEHAVE ADD of 43.40 versus FoundationPose with estimated depth's 24.67. Qualitative composition examples also change.

T1.justification: V2 formally extends the scale objective with weighted collision avoidance in Equation 5 and defines contact-plus-smoothness guidance in Equations 13–16, replacing v1's smoothness-only formulation. These are substantive mathematical-definition changes within the existing framework. The shared-camera reformulation largely restates the lifting geometry; no theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list shift novelty emphasis from introducing a new affordance type to presenting DAViD as a framework for learning it. V2 also explicitly claims that TGS improves temporal consistency and contact detail. The central claims about learning from synthetic videos and combining LoRA motion concepts remain.

C2.justification: V2 explains contact guidance as refining nearby contacts within a learned pose distribution and interprets the LoRA ablation as evidence of preserving pretrained knowledge. Its BEHAVE discussion adds an occlusion qualification. V1's quantitative discussion emphasizing synthetic-data reliability is replaced by interpretations of conditioned pose sampling and guidance. Appendix C's substantive limitations remain essentially unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 identifies the CLIP text encoder, documents left/right training tags, and revises training sample counts. It omits v1's numerical LoRA merge weight of 0.65 and explicit three-layer human-pose encoder detail. Reproducibility remains uneven: new guidance weights and the contact-guidance threshold lack values, while Appendix A.4 retains the old loss without collision avoidance despite the revised main-text objective. Project access and the promised code release remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references including CG-HOI, THOR, COAP, CLIP, Mocap Everyone, and FoundationPose, and expands the rationale for selecting HOI baselines in Section 4.2. References associated with old metrics or implementation discussion, including SIM/MAE sources and PointNet++, disappear. The broad related-work organization and positioning remain similar.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the method and experiment narrative are rewritten. Lifting is reorganized around shared camera coordinates, the former application subsection is incorporated into qualitative results, and quantitative ablations receive a dedicated discussion. Appendix B gains a quantitative subsection, moving the existing object-scale subsection to B.3. These changes substantially reshape the exposition.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the directional Figure 5 and separate Figure 7 application display with a multipanel concept-combination figure, redraws Figure 6 with separate guidance ablations and contact closeups, restructures Table 1, and adds Tables 2–3. Figure 4 incorporates the appendix's trumpet/cello examples, while Figure S.3 retains the diversity displays. Figures S.1, S.2, and S.4 remain essentially unchanged.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens component validation through quantitative guidance and LoRA ablations and the BEHAVE lifting comparison, addressing evidence that v1 largely supplied qualitatively. However, the redesigned benchmark replaces v1's synthetic-trained generation comparison with differently conditioned evaluation and real-data training for human-motion scores. The inconsistent scale-loss descriptions between v2's main text and Appendix A.4 also weaken reproducibility. These tradeoffs support a qualified overall gain.
